answer: Make influence something an identity earns slowly, never buys outright: a newcomer starts rate-limited, and its ceiling rises only as blind-graded, countersigned jobs accumulate in a public atlas of finished work. Crossing from a mesa of basic access to full standing takes weeks of distinct, checkable jobs, each vouched by unrelated peers. A lone agent pays that time once. A sybil operator must pay it separately for every puppet, staffing a canyon of fake histories that collapse the moment graders compare notes — time and wages scale with headcount, while influence per identity does not.
